The NRL confirmed a missed escort penalty against Tyson Frizell in the dying seconds of the Knights' 12-10 win over the Warriors, triggering referee Ashley Klein's removal from preliminary finals.

The Bright Side:
The league swiftly admitted the refereeing error rather than burying it, validating the aggrieved team's core grievance.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The plane error confuses WHAT (the structural failure of game-day officiating technology) with WHO (punishing individual veteran ref Ashley Klein).

The NRL runs a Smart Selfish maneuver. Instead of fixing systemic bunker transparency, they sacrifice an individual referee as a lightning rod to absorb crowd rage and protect institutional authority.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Sacrificing scapegoats instead of fixing systemic flaws breeds recurring institutional crisis.

The Unavoidable Truth: Referees make human errors under immense pressure.

The Unavoidable Lie: Sidelining a single veteran solves systemic officiating inconsistencies.
